findings.description: A Ctrl-C during a batch fetch never stops the batch: `fetchTarget` wraps the killed git's error in a new `Error` with no `signal`, so the batch skips that session and lands the rest.
The PR adds a new exported `interface Landable` directly in land.service.ts, and newly exports the previously private `LandRequest`, so land-batch.service.ts imports both from a service file.
findings.body:
**Exported types are declared in a service file.** This PR adds `export interface Landable` ([L134](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3b16873c74e6026fb76a4f2b6911fb2f2ce1ece4/src/core/land.service.ts#L134-L138)). It also turns the private `interface LandRequest` into `export interface LandRequest` ([L53](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3b16873c74e6026fb76a4f2b6911fb2f2ce1ece4/src/core/land.service.ts#L53)). The new `land-batch.service.ts` imports both.

`docs/conventions/general.md` §Type separation says:

> Exported types live in `*.types.ts` under the area's `types/` folder … **Never inline an exported or reused `type`/`interface` in a `*.service.ts` or `*.routes.ts` file**

The spot-check in `.claude/spot-checks.tsv` (line 8) matches both lines.

The right home already exists: this PR puts the sibling `LandBatchOutcome` in `src/core/types/land.types.ts`. Move `Landable` and `LandRequest` there and import them with `import type`. `PinnedPullRequest`, which `Landable` extends, has to move with them.

findings.description: A Ctrl-C or kill during the batch's audit throws `GateInterruptedError` out of `landSessions`, and `landBatch` in the CLI rethrows it. Which sessions landed, and every refused session's reason, are then never printed, even though the batch already holds them.

In a batch, refusals made before the lock are dropped when the lock is never taken: a lock-wait timeout or `MergeLockHeldError` reaches `refuseScrubbed(error)`, which prints only the lock error. A session already refused before the lock (for example, its PR is CLOSED) is never reported, although ADR 0195 says it is reported with its refusal.

`LandBatchOutcome.refused` doc says a refused session 'landed nothing' and that its own checks refused it. The code also puts lock-lost untried sessions there, and the ADR and `BATCH_UNTOUCHED` say main may already hold a refused session's merge commit.

The `printLanded` JSDoc's second sentence (peers named on stderr 'before its audit started', decision 99) describes the steer and audit mechanics, not what `printLanded` prints. It was moved verbatim from the single-land call site. In a batch the one audit follows every land, so 'its audit' no longer fits.

When the lock is lost after at least one land and before the audit, the batch prints 'Audit skipped: run `pup audit` once after the last land.' That is the `--no-audit` wording. It implies a deliberate skip, when the audit was stopped by the lost lock.

process_issues.description: Ran one security instance, not two, despite the size gate (>400 lines). The trust-boundary surface, the git shell-outs in land.service.ts, is concentrated in one file. Skipped context, spec (no closing issues), workflow-safety (no workflow change) and maintainability (off the default roster).

The reviewer reported a sandbox denial after it misread a saved diff path. As a result it checked the src/core/types/land.types.ts and src/cli/index.ts hunks only through grep, and did not fully audit how thin the CLI stays.

The reviewer did not read the land.service.ts or src/cli/index.ts diffs, so the overlap between the single and batch paths was not assessed. Dropped two of its nits: the `one` closure overrides, which commit 45b87cb declares intentional runtime clearing, and `messageOf`, which the reviewer conceded is not bloat.
